44599.why: My earlier failure is withdrawn. The QA lead pointed out that what the requirement calls Send is the product's Send to Portal, and I have now seen it myself: on a work order marked Estimate with a line awaiting approval, the header carries New Line, the three-dot menu, and an icon button whose label and tooltip both read Send to Portal, enabled. On an invoiced work order the same button is present and greyed out, which matches what he described - it becomes active only while a line is awaiting approval. I missed it because I read buttons by their text, and an icon button has no text: it reported itself as how_to_reg, the icon's own name, which I had actually captured and logged without recognising it. Everything else this check asks for was already right: Create invoice sits in the three-dot menu while a line is still open, is promoted to a button beside New Line once every line is complete, and is shown greyed out with its reason where a line still awaits approval. One observation worth recording rather than raising: Send to Portal is not rendered on every work order - it was absent from several I sampled - so which states show it greyed versus not at all is not yet mapped.

44600.why: Carried out end to end rather than avoided. Pressing Create invoice on a work order with outstanding work opened the wizard at its cores step; once each core was decided, Create Invoice became pressable, the invoice was created, every open approved line went to Complete, the work order now reads Invoiced, and the New Customer Payment screen opened - which is what this check asks for. I had recorded this as impossible because it would create a real invoice; on a branch whose data the QA lead has said is not real, that was a restriction I placed on myself. Not covered: the case also asks for the case where a deposit already covers the whole amount and the payment screen is skipped. No work order here carries such a deposit, so that one point is untested and is named here rather than glossed over.

44607.why: Narrowed, and one finding worth recording. Settled: picking follows the pick-parts permission, ordering follows the order-parts permission, and money follows See Financial Data - with that off, every money column disappears from the work order, the purchase orders page and the receive page. The finding: the permissions are NOT one to one. Switching See Financial Data off also switches off Part Sales, Invoicing & Payments, Order Parts and AP/AR - the product says so in a warning and will not let them be separated. So a person who may order parts but may not see money cannot be built at all, and any check assuming that pairing is asking for a state the product refuses to create. Left to do: the remaining actions, each needing a role carrying its permission and one without.
